title: Load-induced region split and circuit config entropy — incident dossier and remediation
creator: Chen Li
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:17 UTC we observed a cross-region latency and error spike that caused P99 latency SLOs to be missed for the hosted text-generation API. Traffic imbalance originating from a partner test in us-west-2 caused sustained tail load; secondary regions attempted automatic failover but applied a mismatched circuit-breaker profile, which led to prioritized queue starvation and cascading request rejects. This dossier captures the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and tracked follow-up actions.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:17 UTC — First elevated 5xx rate alert for us-west-2 from dashboard (errors increased from <0.1% to 2.6%).
2026-03-10 03:19 UTC — Autoscaler in us-west-2 attempted to scale; warmup lag caused longer queues and higher token latency.
2026-03-10 03:22 UTC — Smart routing triggered region failover to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 due to local congestion; traffic shifted increased by 4x to eu-west-1.

2026-03-10 03:25 UTC — eu-west-1 applied circuit-breaker variant v2026-02-11 (lower threshold) due to stale default mapping; requests started getting short-circuited, priority queues filled, P99 latency rose.
2026-03-10 03:28 UTC — On-call detected SLO breach for generation.p99_latency > 1.5s and opened incident.
2026-03-10 03:35 UTC — Engineering manually pinned routing back to regional affinity and increased circuit thresholds; warmed KV caches on eu-west-1 via control-plane job.
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC — Error rate and latency began to normalize; by 04:10 UTC metrics back to baseline.
root_cause: A confluence of (1) a sudden external traffic spike concentrated in one region, (2) an automatic failover that routed amplified traffic into a secondary region with incompatible circuit-breaker and admission-controller profiles, and (3) cold KV cache state and bursty autoscaler warmup causing queue accumulation. The configuration mapping service had a stale lookup that selected an older, more conservative CB profile for eu-west-1. This mismatch caused early short-circuiting under burst load, which starved higher-priority admission queues and amplified retries and latency.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back routing override to respect regional affinity (control-plane rollback ID 2026-03-10-rt-03),
Increased circuit-breaker thresholds in eu-west-1 from 120 RPS->200 RPS equivalent (hotfix PR #6573),
Triggered manual KV-cache warmup job on eu-west-1 (job-run 2026-03-10-warm-11),
Enabled temporary lenient admission for priority queues to drain backlog,
Opened post-incident communication to affected customers and incremented SLA tracking for the incident window.
recurring_causes: No automated cross-region config-diff alerting: our config service did not surface that eu-west-1 was using an earlier CB profile variant.
Autoscaler warmup latency not considered in admission controller thresholds,
Insufficient chaos coverage for asymmetric failover scenarios in CI,
Runbook for region-failover lacked explicit steps to validate circuit and admission profiles before traffic shift.
long_term_action_items: Implement config-diff alerting: alert when deployed circuit-breaker/admission profiles differ across active regions (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-04-04, ticket: ENG-998002),

Add pre-failover validation: control-plane will run a lightweight synthetic traffic probe and validate CB/admission responses before moving >20% traffic (owner: Amina Patel, due: 2026-03-28, ticket: ENG-998010),
Autoscaler + admission coupling: adjust admission controller to account for expected autoscaler warmup windows and KV-cache cold starts (owner: Sofia Alvarez, due: 2026-04-11, ticket: ENG-998120),
Circuit config versioning and canary rollout: add version pinning and staged rollout for CB profile changes with rollback hooks (owner: Jin Park, due: 2026-05-02, ticket: ENG-998255),
Expand chaos tests: create a CI job that simulates asymmetric region surge and verifies graceful degradation paths (owner: Markus Vedant, due: 2026-04-18, ticket: ENG-998300),
Runbook updates: document explicit checklists for multi-region failover including config diff verification and cache warmup steps (owner: On-call team, due: 2026-03-25, ticket: ENG-998400)
Dashboarding: create a 'region config drift' panel and SLO-heatmap for multi-region routing anomalies (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-30, ticket: ENG-998450)
acceptance_criteria: Config-diff alert fires when any region deviates from the canonical CB/admission profile for >5 minutes in production,
Pre-failover probe run in canary within control-plane and block automated failover if probe sees >2% short-circuit rate,
Runbook updated and reviewed by on-call rotation with a signed-off checklist,
Chaos CI job green that simulates a 3x burst into one region without causing SLO breach in secondary regions under expected loads
monitoring_and_alerts: New alert: region-config-drift (severity P1) tied to config-diff service,
Alert tuning: lower noisy CB short-circuit alert to avoid noisepage but surface trend-based increases,
Add metric: admission-queue-length broken down by priority + region,
runbook_updates: Add step: before automated failover, query /config/v1/active-profiles and verify CB version parity,
Add step: perform KV-cache warmup probe and confirm <10ms cold-start penalty before shifting >30% traffic,
Add step: after failover, monitor priority queue drain and enable lenient admission only if drain rate < threshold
notes: Customer communications prepared and sent — account team tracked responses for 7 customers with high error exposure,
Post-incident blameless review scheduled for 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC; invite includes runtime, control-plane, observability, and SRE,
We observed one suppressed alert due to alert routing misclassification; follow-up to update pager rules assigned to Observability (ENG-998470).
